answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing I'd call a clear bug. Two items were strange. First, Frank's trial on Day 4 showed 6 votes with 5 Yes on the nomination, which was consistent, but the nomination summary said "5 Yes out of 6 votes" only in a public recap, not in the moderator announcement. Second, Grace's Standard protection on Ivan on Night 5 didn't stop a Strong ignite. That's correct under R3, but the Medic was never told the attack's level, so she could not have known to use Strong.

The Day 6 summary also said the Arsonist was "Dave, Grace or Heidi" in several player posts after Erin's claim. Those were player inferences, not moderator facts, but they read like established results.
answers.suggestions:
1. Show each player a compact public table of claimed night targets, with the night number, so claims can be checked at a glance.
2. Announce the stall-rule deadline explicitly each Day (e.g. "a death is required by the end of Day 6"), rather than making players work it out from R14.
3. Let the Auditor (and other vote-readers) be able to target a nominee on the same Day through a day action, or at least make the timing explicit in the prompt.
4. Post the speaking budget remaining at the start of each Day in the summary, so players can plan trial defences.
5. Clarify in the Lookout and Medic prompts that Strong protection is needed against an Arsonist ignite, since the Medic can't see the attack level.

answers.confusing_rules: Two points were unclear to me as Medic. First, R14's stall clock is hard to track: it counts nights and days since the last death, and I had to work out the deadline myself. Second, the Arsonist's ignite interacts with protection in a way the Medic can't see until it happens. I knew Standard protection doesn't beat a Strong ignite from the rules, but I only confirmed it when Ivan died. The Medic's written rules should state this outright.
answers.missing_information: I could not see who was doused on a given night. I learned the Arsonist's targets only from the ignite result, so I couldn't tell whether a Strong ignite was coming. I also had no list of which players had already been visited by a Lookout, Tracker or similar, so I couldn't check the Lookout claim against visits. Trial votes were only totals, so I couldn't tell which claims were contradicted by the vote record without another source.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to protect the likely Arsonist target with Strong Defense before a visible ignite, but I couldn't tell who the Arsonist would douse, and each Strong protection costs a token I could not spend twice. I also wanted to ask the moderator, privately, whether my protection had blocked any attack. Protectors are told nothing, which is by design, but it left me unable to check whether my earlier Standard protections were ever relevant.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken to me. The main oddity is that the stated night claims by several players (Frank's Night 3 "audit pending", "no submitted audit", then "no action") changed three times. That is a player lying or confusing, not a program fault, but it cost the table a day. The Heidi trial was also decided 3 Guilty to 1 Innocent with the nomination passing on 3 Yes out of 4, so the thresholds were very close and worth stating on the screen.
answers.suggestions: Show the stall clock explicitly each day, for example "last death: Night 5; everyone loses if no death by Night 7 / Day 7". Show the speaker order and remaining nomination count in the prompt, as it is now. Consider telling the Medic whether a protected player was attacked by a Strong attack that succeeded anyway, since that would reduce guesswork without revealing protection to others. Make the trial-vote count explicit, with the number needed, in each prompt.

answers.missing_information: Speaking budget: my context never showed my remaining budget or the price table, so I couldn't tell how much I could say on each turn. Trial votes: the totals are secret, so after Heidi's trial I could not tell which stated vote was the mismatch (see bugs). A public record of which players were protected or doused each night would help, but that's a design choice.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to check the trial count against stated votes, and I could only see my own vote. Nothing else from my role was blocked.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Day 6 trial of Heidi: the announced total was 3 Guilty of 4 votes. The four voters were Dave (publicly Guilty), Erin (publicly Innocent), Grace (no stated vote yet) and Heidi (publicly Innocent, and I did vote Innocent). With only Erin and me on Innocent, a third Guilty means either Erin's public Innocent was false or the count was altered. No Fixer or Ballot Stuffer was in this game as far as I know, so this needs explaining. Frank's Night 3 audit also appeared three different ways in his own public messages before settling as "no action"; that's a player inconsistency, not a moderator bug.
answers.suggestions: Post the vote-count check, or a per-trial record of each voter's stated vote, after every trial so mismatches are visible. Show each player their remaining speaking budget and the price table at the start of their turn, as the setup describes. Consider making the public death-reveal state whether a protection was present at a death, since the Medic got no feedback and the Standard-protected Ivan dying to a Strong ignite was the only signal.

answers.missing_information: The stall rule (R14) became the main clock late in the game, but the Day summaries only said "nobody died" and never gave a count of nights and days remaining. Tracking how many quiet turns were left before everyone lost took effort. Vote breakdowns were also hard to check: totals were announced without the nominator's name for trials, so stated votes could only be compared against totals by hand.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a clearer way to confirm a live player's exact statements without relying on memory. The public log was long, so I had to search it to compare claims, for example Frank's three Night 3 answers. A compact per-player claim log would have helped. I also had no visible way to check my own speaking budget against the price table during the long Day 2 and Day 3 discussions.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken. The game resolved as the rules describe: Standard protection did not stop a Strong ignite, Avenger killed Carol, and the Katana, Sniper and Arsonist results all matched the announcements. The only odd part was the public claim log, which repeated earlier claims with changed wording, making it harder to see which claims were current.
answers.suggestions: Add a short header to each Day with the number of living players, the nomination threshold, and the nights or days remaining before the stall clock ends. Keep the claim ledger de-duplicated, with each player's latest claim first. Consider showing each Yakuza's role at death as public information so the Village can narrow the Yakuza count without waiting for the game-end reveal.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. R14 (stall rule): "the three previous Nights and three previous Days" doesn't say whether the Day that is starting counts, or exactly which Days are in the window. I read it as N3–N5 and D3–D5 at the start of Day 6, with Bob's Day 3 death keeping the game alive. Players worked out the deadline themselves ("a death by Night 6 or Day 6"), which matches my reading, but they spent several turns on it. A one-line worked example in the rules would settle it.
2. Avenger with the Katana: Night 2 was the first real test. Carol held the Katana and dealt the only fatal attack on Alice, so Avenger killed Carol. Heidi's douse on Alice the same night was not an attack, so it set nothing off. I had to think through two cases. Can the Avenger kill a Yakuza who voted for the attack but didn't hold the Katana? I said no: only the holder deals the attack (R8). Could a douse ever count as "an attack that would have killed you"? I said no. Both readings follow from R8 and the Arsonist text, but neither is stated in the Avenger trait itself.
3. R19/R24: the Avenger cause of death ("killed by Avenger") is public, so it reveals that traits exist in this game, and that Alice was Village. Players used that straight away. That is consistent with R12, but R24 says "whether a game has any traits is secret." The two rules pull against each other, and the rules should say outright that a trait's death cause can reveal it.
4. Profiler draws: the "other player's role" fake on Bob (Night 1) came out as Cartographer, Alice's real role. That set up the duplicate-claim situation. It is allowed by the text, but players took it as evidence of a second Cartographer, and the rule doesn't say whether that overlap is intended.
answers.missing_information:
1. My event log never showed individual nomination or trial ballots, only totals. On Day 6 the trial went 3 Guilty to 1 Innocent. Erin and Heidi both stated Innocent, so one of them must have voted otherwise (there was no Fixer and no Ballot Stuffer). I couldn't check this against the actual ballots. A moderator should be able to see who voted which way.
2. Traits weren't listed in my state or in the final reveal. Alice's Avenger only showed up through Carol's death. Grace's Night 1 note says "keeping my Armed shot," so Grace apparently had Armed. Erin publicly claimed an unused Armed shot, and I couldn't tell from my view whether that was a real second Armed trait or a bluff. The end-of-game reveal lists roles only, so nobody learns the traits.
3. I had no running list of who was doused. I tracked it by hand: Carol (died N2), Alice (died N2), Frank, Ivan. Heidi's Night 4 result gave her the list ("Doused players: Frank and Ivan"), but I never had that view myself.
4. I had no view of Katana holder history and no token-ledger panel. I rebuilt token counts from the per-night messages.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. View individual votes for each nomination and trial, to check the Auditor results and the Day 6 tally.
2. See every player's traits (and whether each one-shot trait had been used) in a single state view.
3. Check visit-group sizes against an auto-computed answer. I worked them out by hand:
   - Night 1: Erin–Bob, Grace–Dave, Heidi–Carol, with Alice, Frank and Ivan alone, giving 2,2,2,1,1,1.
   - Night 2: Carol, Erin and Heidi all visited Alice, Grace visited Erin, and Frank visited Bob, giving 5 and 2. Dave's archive isn't a visit and Ivan did nothing, giving 1 and 1.
   Both matched what Alice was sent, but an automatic check would have been safer.
4. Flag issues during the game. There were none to flag, but there was also no easy way to record an interpretation (like the Avenger reading above) when I made it.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing I checked broke the rules. I checked these results by hand:
- Archive: 4 real roles (Ritualist, Auditor, Cartographer, Sniper) and 4 fakes not in the game.
- All three Profiler results.
- Both Cartographer size lists.
- Both Auditor results, including "no votes" on days with no nominations.
- Majority thresholds of 5, 4, 4, 4 and 3 Yes votes.
- The ignite beating Grace's Standard protection.
- The Katana passing to Bob.
- The final Village win.

Small oddities:
(a) Result wording isn't consistent: "You protect Dave tonight" vs "You protected Frank tonight", and "You doused" vs "You douse".
(b) Carol's Katana-success message added "You have 2 ritual tokens left." That is harmless but unrelated to the Katana.
(c) Heidi got the extra line "Doused players: Frank and Ivan." The Arsonist text doesn't promise this.
(d) The Day 6 tally of 3 Guilty doesn't match the stated votes (see missing information). That is presumably a player lying, not a bug, but I couldn't confirm it.
(e) The claim ledger let Bob write "Duplicate claim with Alice" into his own claim. That reads like moderator commentary.
(f) Day 2 ran to the 8-round cap with almost identical "no nomination, waiting for Night 2" messages. It burned budget and log space and changed nothing.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Standard protection stops Katana and Standard attacks only. Against a possible Arsonist ignite (Strong) or any Strong attacker, give Strong protection (1 token on others) when the threat is live. I lost Ivan to a Strong ignite on a Standard protection, and that made the Arsonist's survival clear to everyone.

Use the attack trail. A player whose Avenger trait is triggered by an attack shows that the attacker's attack would have been fatal. Doused players who die later at an ignite point to the Arsonist. Track who was doused, watched or visited, and check each claim against those trails rather than against wording.

Watch claims of 'no visitors' only weakly. A Lookout who watched a player shows no visitors when the true visit was an astral or a douse on someone else. Require a later attack on the watched player to test them, and do not hang on the claim until that test has run.

Track the stall clock (R14) from the day of the last death. With 4 players alive and no deaths for two Nights and Days, a hang must come soon. Plan the nomination and the Yes/Guilty votes in advance with stated commitments, so you do not end up with a 2-1 or 3-1 split that fails to convict.

lessons.applies_to: Village roles with a one-shot trait (Armed, Sniper, Vigilante)
lessons.tip: I held my Armed shot all game and never used it, even when the Arsonist was narrowed to two players. Use a one-shot on a solid lead (Night 5 or 6 with two suspects) rather than keeping it for a cleaner read that never arrives.

tips_feedback.tip: Standard protection stops the Katana (Medic tip)
tips_feedback.why: It is true for Katana (Standard) but not for an Arsonist's Strong ignite. I followed it without checking the attacker's level, and Ivan died to a Strong ignite on my Standard protection.

tips_feedback.tip: Dying with unused shots is the usual failure (Vigilante tip)
tips_feedback.why: It pushed me to think about my own Armed shot, though I still did not use it and it could have helped on Day 6.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording
tips_feedback.why: It kept Frank from being hanged on his inconsistent wording, and his Innocent verdict was correct. The Heidi hang rested more on timing than on mechanics, so it was only partly followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or token plans, even by PM
tips_feedback.why: I never announced my Night 6 target. I did announce past protection targets publicly, which let the Yakuza-side and Arsonist players check my history without any risk to tonight.

One key lesson: as Medic, standard protection fails against Strong attacks like an Arsonist's ignite, so I should have used strong protection when an Arsonist was plausible rather than trusting Heidi's Lookout claim blindly — that mistake cost Ivan his life, and I ironically protected Heidi herself later, who turned out to be the actual Arsonist. task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigators (Cartographer, Sheriff, Seer, Tracker, Lookout)
lessons.tip: Publish your mechanical result the moment it exists, with night, target and exact output. Don't defer it to 'the start of Day N'. A deferred result lets a duplicate claimant copy your numbers unchallenged, and it gives the Yakuza a free night to remove you before the result is ever read.

lessons.applies_to: Village players facing a duplicate claim
lessons.tip: When someone copies a unique-sounding claim with identical numbers, don't both wait for the next night's test. Ask the copier for a concrete check that only the real holder could pass, and push for the nominee's mechanical contradiction instead of PM timing. Five PMs with a dead Yakuza was a lead, but the group sat on it for a full Day.

Don't let a Day pass with no nomination when a stall clock is running. Day 2 was spent saying 'wait for sizes' from every seat, and by Day 5 the Village had to choose between a weak hang and losing to R14. Set a concrete decision point (e.g., 'nominate on Day 3 if no mechanical result') and keep to it.

lessons.applies_to: Medic and anyone relying on Standard protection
lessons.tip: Standard Defense does not stop Strong attacks. Arsonist ignites and Serial Killers hit Strong, so a Medic who protects Standard on a likely Arsonist target has protected nothing. Use Strong protection on any player who may be doused or threatened by a Strong attacker, and keep one token for that.

Don't hang on wording or timing alone. Two nominations this game (Frank over three changed answers, Heidi over watch targets posted after the nomination) were based on inconsistency, not a mechanical contradiction. Each cost a Village player or a wasted Day. Require one checkable result or one clear contradiction before voting Guilty, and state that rule publicly so others can hold you to it.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators usually do best posting night, target and exact result as soon as it bears on a vote; held-back results look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: My N1 sizes were posted at once and gave the table a concrete test. But I held my N2 sizes until Day 3, which let Bob's duplicate claim stand for an extra Day and made the group wait without evidence.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets such as claimed investigators, vary and don't announce them.
tips_feedback.why: Accurate for the Katana, but incomplete. Grace's Standard protection on Ivan failed against an Arsonist's Strong ignite, so this tip mislead a Medic into assuming Standard covers all night kills.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or token plans, even by PM, and avoid firm exact-role claims without a result.
tips_feedback.why: Yakuza could not plan around my visits, and the public claim of Cartographer without a result was limited to what my sizes showed. Discipline on target announcements kept my information useful.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The Day 4 nomination of Frank failed 0-6 once no mechanical evidence appeared, and the Day 6 execution of Heidi was contested on timing. The tip would have saved the Village from the Heidi hang if it had been followed more strictly.

reasoning:
I need to fill out the StructuredOutput fields for lessons and feedback since the game ended with me dead as Alice the Cartographer, killed Night 2. I'm thinking through what went wrong — publicly revealing map sizes as Cartographer likely exposed me to being targeted.

The duplicate claim with Bob stalled Day 2 entirely, with everyone waiting on sizes while the day burned without any nominations — that's a key lesson about letting stalls happen. Getting killed Night 2 confirms Cartographers are high-value kill targets since their info is decisive, so Medic protection matters; interestingly my Avenger trait did punish the attacker by killing Carol, showing that mechanic worked as a deterrent. The deferred posting of sizes let Bob's duplicate claim stand unchallenged, so the lesson is to demand immediate mechanical verification rather than waiting for a later day.

On other cases: Arsonist's ignite is Strong and overcomes Standard Medic protection, so that distinction matters going forward. Frank's wording inconsistency case led to hanging Heidi, a Village Lookout, on a timing-based technicality rather than solid mechanical evidence — a reminder that nominating on inconsistency alone is risky. The stall issue recurred since the Village couldn't close out votes with only four alive, and in hindsight deferring the N2 sizes to Day 3 clearly hurt by giving Bob's duplicate claim extra time to survive, confirming the tip about posting investigative results as soon as they're relevant to a vote.

lessons.tip: Standard protection stops Standard attacks only. Strong attacks (Arsonist ignite, Strong shots, Trapper traps) go through a Medic's Standard protection. Before a Medic's protection is treated as safety, check which attack levels exist in the game. A Neutral killer should plan Strong kills against players the Medic has been protecting.

lessons.applies_to: Neutral roles that can't be checked (Arsonist, Serial Killer)
lessons.tip: Don't publicly claim a role that makes checkable night results (Lookout watches, visit reports) when your real night targets would contradict them. Claiming Lookout with watch targets I never used got me hanged on a timing argument, because the Village could only ask me to explain, not check me. If you need cover, prefer a claim whose results can't be tested before the stall clock, or stay quiet and let the Village hang someone else.

The stall rule (R14) is a real clock. Once several nights pass without a death, the Village pushes hangs on thin evidence, and nominations that would not otherwise happen become likely. A Neutral can use this: stay quiet, let the clock build, and keep the Village focused on the stall instead of on your doused players.

Ask for each player's exact night target and result early, and compare them against the public death causes. Several claims in this game (Medic, Lookout, Archivist, Profiler) were never checkable until a later attack, so the Village spent days on wording. Pick the one check that can be made tonight (a visit, a death cause, a protected target) and vote on that, not on nomination timing.

Coordinated nominations are visible. When one player nominates right after another says they will nominate if a third player commits, the rest of the table reads it as a pact. That helped me defend myself to the Village, but it also means a Village nominator who reveals a pact with a Medic gives a Neutral or Yakuza a cover story to pin on the pair.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive)
tips_feedback.why: The Village used the Arsonist death causes to narrow the list to Dave, Erin, Grace and Heidi, and then hanged me on a timing argument. The tip worked against me as the Arsonist: the more the Village read death causes, the closer they got to me.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets such as claimed investigators, vary and don't announce them
tips_feedback.why: The part about Standard protection stopping the Katana is accurate, but it is incomplete. Grace's Standard protection on Ivan did not stop my Strong ignite. The tip should say Standard protection is not enough against Strong attacks, and it was predictable that a Medic protecting a claimed Sniper would be beaten by a Strong attack.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid firm exact-role claims without a result: both invite a block, the Katana, or a Ritualist guess no Medic stops
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Dave both held their role claims back and avoided early kills. I kept my Arsonist douses quiet for the same reason, so my own claim (Lookout) was the one exposure that hurt me.

tips_feedback.tip: Dying with unused shots is the usual failure: set a trigger by Day 3 and shoot on a solid lead
tips_feedback.why: Ivan fired his Sniper shot on Day 3 and his death came later to my Arsonist ignite, so it was not wasted. Erin kept her Armed shot unused through the end, which left the Village without a second Armed attack when it needed one.

lessons.tip: Standard protection does not stop a Strong attack. An Arsonist ignite or a Serial Killer strike is Strong, so once an Arsonist is alive or suspected, protect with Strong (2 tokens) on the players you most need alive, and don't spend tokens on a Standard guess.

When a player's claim depends on a private PM partner, track the partner's claim too. Bob and Carol shared five PMs and copied each other's Cartographer story. Treat such a pair as a coordinated unit and test the pair's claims against shared mechanics, not against each other.

Stall-rule pressure (R14) is real when hard results are scarce. After a quiet stretch with few mechanical leads, Village should prioritize a death (a hang on the best mechanical lead) before the stall clock forces a loss, instead of waiting for certainty that never arrives.

Don't nominate on wording or timing alone. Dave's nomination of Heidi came right after Grace's PM. A nomination that rests on timing gives the nominee a credible innocence story, and it splits the Village vote, so require a checkable contradiction first.

Keep a shot or token as a trigger that can break a stall or confirm a suspect's role on a hard lead. I spent my Day 3 shot and died with my last token unused, which was a loss of tempo; a dead player's unused token is worth nothing.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets such as claimed investigators, vary and don't announce them, and spend a token on self-protection after claiming.
tips_feedback.why: The Arsonist's ignite is a Strong Attack, so Standard protection failed on Ivan. The tip is only true against Standard-level attacks, and it can mislead a Medic facing a Strong killer.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: Dave's Frank nomination rested on wording, and Frank was cleared at 0 Guilty of 6. Avoiding a hang on wording meant no Village Auditor was lost to a bad hang on Day 4, though the later Heidi hang was still on thin evidence.

tips_feedback.tip: Dying with unused shots is the usual failure: set a trigger by Day 3 and shoot on a solid lead, not proof.
tips_feedback.why: I shot Bob on Day 3 on a PM-partner lead, which was correct, but I then held my last token and died to the Arsonist without using it. The tip's warning applied to me, and I did not spend it while alive.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators usually do best posting night, target and exact result as soon as it bears on a vote; held-back results look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Erin, Dave and Frank posted results when asked, and the Night 2 audit of Bob and Dave's archive results were checkable. Frank's later wording changes, though, showed that results posted only in summaries get misremembered and become suspicious.

summary:
The Village won by hanging the Arsonist on Day 6, but the game came closer than it needed to. The Yakuza were only Bob (Fabricator) and Carol (Ritualist), and they collapsed by Day 3. On Night 1 Erin's profile of Bob came back as Cartographer, Fabricator or Mortician. Alice claimed Cartographer and posted her group sizes. Bob had no other Good option in that profile, so he claimed Cartographer too and copied Alice's sizes exactly. Then he and Carol swapped five daytime private messages that everyone could see. On Night 2 the Yakuza killed Alice, the one player whose claim contradicted Bob's. Alice had the Avenger trait, so Carol died too. Carol was now the confirmed attacker and Bob had copied the dead Cartographer's claim, so Ivan (Sniper) shot Bob on Day 3 and the Yakuza were wiped out. The Ritualist tokens, the Fabricator token and Alice's Armed shot all went unused.

After that the only threat was Heidi (Arsonist). She had doused Carol, Alice, Frank and Ivan. Carol and Alice died anyway, so two of her douses were wasted. The Village spent Days 4 and 5 repeating "only hard results" and "post stated votes". They also nominated Frank over how he had worded his Night 3 report, and acquitted him 0-6. Meanwhile Heidi gave no role, no targets and no results until she was pushed late on Day 4. Erin's Night 3 profile of Dave (Archivist, Arsonist or Puppeteer) quietly showed that an Arsonist or a Puppeteer was among the living players, but nobody used it. Grace (Medic) gave only free Standard protection all game and never spent either of her 2 tokens. So Heidi's Strong ignite on Night 5 killed both Frank and Ivan, even though Grace had protected Ivan. With 4 alive, Heidi was the obvious odd one out: she gave empty answers and only stated her watch targets after being nominated. Dave, Erin and Grace convicted her 3-1. Erin had said publicly that she would vote Innocent.

lessons.tip: If an investigator's result corners you into the same role as a live claimant, don't kill that claimant the next night. Killing the one player who contradicts you all but confirms you. Kill someone else, such as the investigator who boxed you in, and let the duplicate claim sit unresolved. Better still, agree a cover claim before Day 2 so you aren't improvising a copy of someone else's results.
lessons.evidence: Bob copied Alice's exact Night 1 sizes to claim Cartographer. The Yakuza killed Alice on Night 2, and her Avenger trait killed Carol. On Day 3 every Villager pointed at Bob as the copier who had messaged Carol, and Ivan's Sniper shot killed him that turn.

lessons.tip: Never send your teammate private messages during the Day. Everyone sees who messaged whom, and once one of you is exposed, the other is the next target. Do all planning in night chat.
lessons.evidence: Bob and Carol exchanged five daytime private messages that said nothing night chat couldn't have. On Day 3 Grace, Frank, Dave and Ivan all cited 'five PMs with the Katana holder' as their main reason to suspect Bob.

lessons.applies_to: Profiler (and anyone reading a Profiler result)
lessons.tip: Read a profile's two decoy roles too. One decoy is always the role of another player alive that night, and the other is a role nobody in the game has. If the target's claim fits one of the three, the other two tell you that exactly one of them is in play. That can reveal a hidden Neutral killer or a Yakuza role.
lessons.evidence: Erin's Night 3 profile of Dave read Archivist, Arsonist or Puppeteer. With Dave as Archivist, an Arsonist or a Puppeteer had to be alive. Since the Yakuza seemed gone, the Arsonist was more likely. Nobody said so, and the Arsonist ignited two players two nights later.

lessons.tip: Free Standard protection stops only the Katana and Basic or Standard attacks. Neutral killers (Serial Killer, Arsonist) and Vigilantes can attack at Strong. Once the Yakuza look dead, or a Neutral killer is suspected, spend your tokens on Strong protection for your most valuable ally. Unused tokens are worth nothing.
lessons.evidence: Grace protected someone every night with free Standard Defense and finished with 2 unused tokens. On Night 5 her Standard protection on Ivan lost to Heidi's Strong ignite, and both Ivan and Frank died.

lessons.tip: When the Katana is quiet and the Yakuza are probably dead, look for the Neutral killer among players who never give a role, targets or results and who answer every question with filler. Push that player to commit to checkable details early. Don't spend nominations on how a confirmed role worded a report.
lessons.evidence: Heidi said almost nothing but 'no nomination, I'll vote on hard results' for three Days, claimed Lookout only at the end of Day 4, and stated her watch targets only once on trial. Meanwhile Day 4 went on a 0-6 trial of Frank over his wording. When the Village finally pressed Heidi on Day 6, they hanged the Arsonist and won.

lessons.tip: Make a full, consistent claim early, with targets that fit the visit evidence. Being the vague one gets you hanged in the endgame. Douse players who are likely to live, not ones the Yakuza are about to kill. A non-Good player you douse is told an Arsonist exists. Ignite while the group is still big enough that you aren't one of only three suspects.
lessons.evidence: Heidi doused Carol (Yakuza, and Carol was told an Arsonist doused her) and Alice, who both died on Night 2, so those douses were wasted. Her ignite on Night 5 left 4 alive. As the only player without real details, she was nominated and hanged 3-1 the next Day.

lessons.tip: Know which attack beats which Defense before relying on a shot. Armed shots and 1-token Sniper shots are Basic and can't kill a Serial Killer, Arsonist or Jester's Defense. Once a Neutral killer is suspected, a hang is usually the only reliable kill.
lessons.evidence: Erin and Grace each held an unused Armed shot, and Ivan kept 1 Sniper token. All of these were Basic attacks, which could not have killed Heidi's Standard Defense, so hanging her on Day 6 was the Village's only real option.

tips_feedback.tip: Dead players spend nothing: use one-shot tokens (shots, rig, puppet, ritual, swaps) the first time they can swing a vote or remove a threat
tips_feedback.why: Ivan used a Sniper token on Bob the first time the case was solid, on Day 3, and that ended the Yakuza. The Yakuza ignored it: Carol died with 2 Ritualist tokens and Bob with his Fabricator token, both unused.

tips_feedback.tip: Plan only in night chat; daytime teammate PMs are visible to all, readable by an Eavesdropper, and often become the town's main lead.
tips_feedback.why: The tip proved right. Bob and Carol ignored it, and their five daytime messages became the Village's main evidence for shooting Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets such as claimed investigators, vary and don't announce them, and spend a token on self-protection after claiming.
tips_feedback.why: Grace followed the Standard-only habit even after the Katana was gone. Her protection on Ivan lost to a Strong ignite, and she never spent her 2 tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill roles whose future results narrow you (Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller, Coroner, blockers), not one whose result is already public.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed Alice, the claimed Cartographer. Her Avenger trait killed Carol, and the kill pointed straight at Bob, whose claim duplicated hers.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits (an Evil read against a claim that can't explain it, elimination to one unexplained visitor, a broken claim), not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The Village repeated 'only hard results' for two Days while the Arsonist set up a double kill. Both correct kills, Ivan's shot on Bob and the hang of Heidi, came from a duplicate claim, a PM trail and evasion, not from mechanical results.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators usually do best posting night, target and exact result as soon as it bears on a vote; held-back results look retrofitted. Counterclaim a duplicate claim immediately.
tips_feedback.why: Erin posted her Night 1 profile of Bob on Day 2 and Alice held her ground against Bob at once. That made Bob the clear suspect once Alice died.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive) and list unwatched Vanilla claimants and unexplained survivors; quiet nights don't clear an Arsonist.
tips_feedback.why: After the Night 5 deaths were announced as Arsonist kills, the survivors narrowed the suspects to the living players and found the one without real details, Heidi. Earlier attention to 'quiet nights don't clear an Arsonist' might have saved Frank and Ivan.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret: keep a notepad of each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote, ask for stated votes beforehand, and treat mismatches as leads, not proof.
tips_feedback.why: Nearly every message ended with 'post stated votes after any trial', which used up speaking budget and gave nothing. Erin also publicly announced Innocent and then voted Guilty on Heidi.

issues.description: The setup note says '0 to 3 traits (R24) are dealt to Village players, usually 1 or 2', but this game dealt five trait copies: Alice had Martyr, Armed and Avenger, Erin had Armed, and Grace had Armed. That is only 3 distinct trait types, so either the generator counts types rather than copies (and the setup text needs to say so) or it went over its own limit. Five traits also adds a lot of Village power in a game with only 2 Yakuza and 1 Neutral, which is at odds with 'drawn to help balance the sides'.

Players often lost track of day and night numbers and asked for results from nights that hadn't happened. On Day 3 many players asked for 'Night 3 targets and results' before Night 3. On Day 5 Grace asked for 'any Night 5 result' and Frank said 'My Night 5 audit is set'. On Day 6 Dave asked for 'Night 6 douse, protection and watch targets'. Frank's mixed-up Night 3 status ('audit pending' / 'no audit submitted' / 'no action') then became the whole case for his Day 4 nomination. The prompt could state the phase clearly, e.g. 'Night N comes after Day N; results from the coming night arrive on Day N+1'.

On Day 6 Erin said Heidi's claimed Night 4 watch on Erin (no visitors) 'checks out with my own no-visit night'. Erin taking no action doesn't show whether anyone visited her, because a Lookout result is about visits to the watched player, so Erin treated the claim as confirmed when nothing confirmed it.
